subproblem.title: Countable atlas of flattening charts on {y ∈ V : DF(y) ≠ 0} (inverse function theorem; parent step 2)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Euclid (n + 1) → ℝ) (V : Set (Euclid (n + 1))), IsOpen V → ContDiff ℝ 1 F → ∃ (Ω : ℕ → Set (Euclid (n + 1))) (Θ : ℕ → Euclid (n + 1) → Euclid (n + 1)), (∀ k, IsOpen (Ω k) ∧ ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (Θ k) (Ω k) ∧ InjOn (Θ k) (Ω k) ∧ (∀ z ∈ Ω k, Injective (fderiv ℝ (Θ k) z)) ∧ IsOpen (Θ k '' Ω k) ∧ Θ k '' Ω k ⊆ V ∧ ∀ z ∈ Ω k, F (Θ k z) = z 0) ∧ {y | y ∈ V ∧ fderiv ℝ F y ≠ 0} ⊆ ⋃ k, Θ k '' Ω k
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof: local straightening Φ_{y₀} = (F, π_{y₀}) of F on the regular part by the inverse function theorem, and the countable choice of charts by second countability. Here Θ_k is the local inverse Φ_k⁻¹ and Ω_k = Φ_k(W_k).

Notation: ℝ^k = Euclid k with coordinates z_0, …, z_{k−1}; DF(y) = fderiv ℝ F y.

1. Local flattening map. Fix y₀ ∈ V with DF(y₀) ≠ 0. The nonzero linear functional DF(y₀) : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ is surjective, so K₀ := ker DF(y₀) has dimension n by rank–nullity. Choose a basis (u_1, …, u_n) of K₀; the parent uses an orthonormal basis of ∇F(y₀)^⊥ = K₀, but any basis works. Define Φ : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1} by Φ(y)_0 := F(y) and Φ(y)_i := ⟨u_i, y⟩ for i = 1, …, n. Each coordinate is C¹, so Φ is C¹ with DΦ(y)h = (DF(y)h, ⟨u_1, h⟩, …, ⟨u_n, h⟩).
2. DΦ(y₀) is invertible. If DΦ(y₀)h = 0, then DF(y₀)h = 0, so h ∈ K₀. Also ⟨u_i, h⟩ = 0 for all i, so h is orthogonal to span(u_1, …, u_n) = K₀, which contains h. Hence |h|² = 0 and h = 0. An injective linear endomorphism of ℝ^{n+1} is invertible. Let L₀ be DΦ(y₀) regarded as a continuous linear equivalence; Φ has derivative L₀ at y₀.
3. Inverse function theorem. Φ is C¹ at y₀ with invertible derivative L₀. Mathlib ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph (file Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/InverseFunctionTheorem/ContDiff.lean, smoothness 1) gives an open partial homeomorphism e of ℝ^{n+1} with these properties:
   - its underlying function is Φ, and y₀ ∈ e.source;
   - e.source and e.target = e(e.source) are open;
   - e.symm(e(y)) = y for y ∈ e.source;
   - e(e.symm(z)) = z and e.symm(z) ∈ e.source for z ∈ e.target.
4. Shrinking. The set I := {y : det DΦ(y) ≠ 0}, where DΦ(y) is invertible, is open because y ↦ DΦ(y) and det are continuous, and it contains y₀. Put W := e.source ∩ V ∩ I, an open set containing y₀. Put Ω := e(W) = Φ(W) and Θ := e.symm, regarded as a map ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{n+1}. Ω is open because a partial homeomorphism maps open subsets of its source to open sets (Mathlib OpenPartialHomeomorph.isOpen_image_of_subset_source).
5. Properties of (Ω, Θ).
   (i) Θ(Ω) = W, since Θ(Φ(y)) = e.symm(e(y)) = y for y ∈ W. Hence Θ(Ω) is open, contains y₀ and is contained in V.
   (ii) Θ is injective on Ω, because Ω ⊆ e.target and e.symm is injective on e.target.
   (iii) Let z ∈ Ω, say z = Φ(y) with y ∈ W; then Θ(z) = y and Φ(Θ(z)) = z. Since y ∈ I, DΦ(y) is invertible; call it L as a continuous linear equivalence. The C¹ inverse function theorem for partial homeomorphisms (Mathlib OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm, applied to e at z ∈ e.target, using HasFDerivAt e L (e.symm z) and e C¹ at e.symm z = y) shows Θ is C¹ at z. By Mathlib OpenPartialHomeomorph.hasFDerivAt_symm, Θ has derivative L⁻¹ at z, so DΘ(z) = L⁻¹ is injective. Since Ω is open and Θ is C¹ at each point of Ω, Θ is C¹ on Ω.
   (iv) For z ∈ Ω, F(Θ(z)) = Φ(Θ(z))_0 = z_0.
6. Countably many charts. Let R := {y ∈ V : DF(y) ≠ 0}.
   - If R = ∅, put Ω_k := ∅ and Θ_k := id for all k. Every chart requirement holds vacuously (Θ_k(∅) = ∅ is open and contained in V), and R ⊆ ⋃_k Θ_k(Ω_k) holds trivially.
   - Otherwise, steps 1–5 give for every y₀ ∈ R a pair (Ω_{y₀}, Θ_{y₀}) satisfying all chart requirements, with y₀ ∈ Θ_{y₀}(Ω_{y₀}) open. These open sets cover R. ℝ^{n+1} is second countable, so countably many of them already cover R (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable, or IsLindelof.indexed_countable_subcover). Enumerate this nonempty countable family as k ↦ (Ω_k, Θ_k), repetitions allowed.
   By step 5 each (Ω_k, Θ_k) satisfies all the chart requirements: Ω_k is open; Θ_k is C¹ and injective on Ω_k with injective derivative; Θ_k(Ω_k) is open and contained in V; F(Θ_k(z)) = z_0 on Ω_k. Also {y ∈ V : DF(y) ≠ 0} ⊆ ⋃_k Θ_k(Ω_k). ∎
proof_key_steps: At y₀ ∈ V with DF(y₀) ≠ 0, Φ(y) = (F(y), ⟨u_1, y⟩, …, ⟨u_n, y⟩) with (u_i) a basis of ker DF(y₀) has invertible derivative at y₀.
C¹ inverse function theorem (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph); shrink the source to W = source ∩ V ∩ {DΦ invertible}; put Ω = Φ(W) (open) and Θ = local inverse.
Θ is C¹ and injective on Ω with DΘ(z) = DΦ(Θz)⁻¹ injective, Θ(Ω) = W is open and contained in V, and F(Θ(z)) = Φ(Θ(z))_0 = z_0.
Second countability gives countably many such charts covering {y ∈ V : DF(y) ≠ 0}; use empty charts when that set is empty.

audit.reason: The explicit flattening map has invertible derivative at each regular point. The inverse function theorem, source restriction and countable subcover prove every chart property and the coverage conclusion. The empty regular locus is handled.
